records.real_world_identity_notes: The Assetto Corsa EVO roster identifies the content as Honda S-2000 (2003). Honda's exact 2003 archive identifies the production S2000 as type LA-AP1 and documents the F20C engine, six-speed manual, dry single-plate diaphragm clutch, constant-mesh transmission, and floor-shift operation. This is the road-going 2003 AP1 S2000, not the later AP2/F22C configuration, an AP1 facelift from another model year, a Type V with variable-ratio steering, or an aftermarket/race conversion.

records.specification_basis: Honda explicitly instructs the driver to push the clutch pedal all the way down when shifting up or down. Honda's 2003 specification lists a six-speed manual transmission, and the owner's manual identifies the six-speed manual and its first-through-sixth shift sequence. Honda's 2003 specification calls the transmission constant-mesh, and the 2003 owner's manual explicitly says the manual transmission is synchronized in all forward gears. Honda specifies floor-shift operation, and the exact-year owner's manual documents the manual gearshift lever's multi-plane gate and reverse lockout. Together these establish a driver-operated H-pattern floor shifter rather than a sequential or paddle system. The 2003 owner's manual's gearshift-lever section identifies the six forward gears in the conventional 1-2 through 5-6 gate and separately describes reverse beside the neutral gate, establishing the standard H pattern. Honda's exact-year starting procedure requires the clutch pedal to be pushed all the way down before the engine can be started, and the car uses a conventional dry manual clutch. Honda explicitly states that the clutch pedal must be pushed all the way down when shifting up or down.
